original_question: Determine the type t(S) of a numerical semigroup S from other standard invariants, especially the multiplicity m(S), embedding dimension e(S), genus g(S), or Frobenius number F(S).
target_in_paper: Section 1, “Notable elements and first problems”: the unnumbered open research direction stated immediately after the definition of pseudo-Frobenius numbers and type, namely to determine the type of a numerical semigroup once invariants such as multiplicity, embedding dimension, genus, or Frobenius number are fixed. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s target invariant (the type of a numerical semigroup) and the same four comparison invariants explicitly named in the paper: multiplicity, embedding dimension, genus, and Frobenius number. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
missing_details: The draft should define a numerical semigroup: a subset S of ℕ that contains 0, is closed under addition, and has finite complement in ℕ. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
It should define the type via pseudo-Frobenius numbers: PF(S) = {x ∈ ℕ ∖ S : x + s ∈ S for every nonzero s ∈ S}, and t(S) = |PF(S)|. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

It should define the comparison invariants explicitly: m(S) = min(S ∖ {0}), e(S) = the cardinality of the unique minimal system of generators of S, g(S) = |ℕ ∖ S|, and F(S) = max(ℕ ∖ S). ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

To match the paper more faithfully, the quantifier should be stated as: for prescribed admissible values of one or more of these invariants, determine or characterize the possible values of t(S). The paper does not say that t(S) is necessarily a single-valued function of any one invariant. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

Nearby context worth making explicit: the paper records e(S) = 2 ⇒ t(S) = 1, e(S) = 3 ⇒ t(S) ∈ {1,2}, while for e(S) ≥ 4 the type can be arbitrarily large; it also states the general bounds t(S) ≤ m(S) − 1 and t(S) + 1 ≤ g(S). These facts explain why the question should be phrased as determining possible types under fixed invariants, not as recovering a unique formula in complete generality. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, or nilpotency hypothesis is part of this problem; it is a purely numerical-semigroup question. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
refined_question: For a numerical semigroup S ⊆ ℕ, let PF(S) = {x ∈ ℕ ∖ S : x + s ∈ S for every nonzero s ∈ S} be its set of pseudo-Frobenius numbers, and let t(S) = |PF(S)| be its type. If one fixes admissible values of one or more standard invariants of S—its multiplicity m(S) = min(S ∖ {0}), embedding dimension e(S) equal to the number of elements in the unique minimal system of generators of S, genus g(S) = |ℕ ∖ S|, and Frobenius number F(S) = max(ℕ ∖ S)—determine or characterize the possible values of t(S). ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper: it appears in Section 1 immediately after the definition of type and after the nearby facts that motivate the question. I sharpened your draft only enough to make it stand alone: I added the definitions of numerical semigroup, pseudo-Frobenius number, type, multiplicity, embedding dimension, genus, and Frobenius number, and I changed “determine t(S) from” to “determine or characterize the possible values of t(S) for prescribed invariants,” because the surrounding context shows that fixed invariants do not automatically force a unique value in general. Section 6 confirms that the embedding-dimension-three case is already largely understood in the paper’s background discussion, so the intended target is the broader unnumbered Section 1 problem rather than a later specialized subsection. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
